## The discovery

For much of its early history, *South Park* primarily followed Stan, Kyle, Cartman, and Kenny. The transcript data points to a striking change in dialogue prominence: Randy Marsh's share rises as Stan Marsh's share declines.

## The evidence

This interactive chart compares Randy and Stan's recorded dialogue lines as a share of all transcript lines in each season. Hover over a point to see the season's line count and share. The data comes from the [`southparkr` package](https://github.com/pdrhlik/southparkr) and covers seasons 1-21 (1997-2017).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(southparkr)
library(plotly)

dialogue_lines <- episode_lines |>
  mutate(character = str_remove_all(character, "[:\"]"))

season_totals <- dialogue_lines |>
  count(season_number, name = "all_lines")

seasons <- sort(unique(dialogue_lines$season_number))

randy_stan_by_season <- dialogue_lines |>
  filter(character %in% c("Randy", "Stan")) |>
  count(season_number, character, name = "lines") |>
  complete(
    season_number = seasons,
    character = c("Randy", "Stan"),
    fill = list(lines = 0)
  ) |>
  left_join(season_totals, by = "season_number") |>
  mutate(
    share = 100 * lines / all_lines,
    period = case_when(
      season_number <= 7 ~ "Early",
      season_number <= 14 ~ "Middle",
      TRUE ~ "Later"
    ),
    character_label = recode(character, Randy = "Randy Marsh", Stan = "Stan Marsh")
  )

period_shares <- randy_stan_by_season |>
  group_by(period, character) |>
  summarise(mean_share = mean(share), .groups = "drop")

randy_early_share <- period_shares |>
  filter(period == "Early", character == "Randy") |>
  pull(mean_share)
randy_later_share <- period_shares |>
  filter(period == "Later", character == "Randy") |>
  pull(mean_share)
stan_early_share <- period_shares |>
  filter(period == "Early", character == "Stan") |>
  pull(mean_share)
stan_later_share <- period_shares |>
  filter(period == "Later", character == "Stan") |>
  pull(mean_share)

randy_stan_plot <- randy_stan_by_season |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = season_number,
    y = share,
    color = character_label,
    group = character_label,
    text = paste(
      "Season:", season_number,
      "<br>Character:", character_label,
      "<br>Transcript lines:", lines,
      "<br>Share of all lines:", round(share, 2), "%"
    )
  )) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seasons) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Randy's dialogue share rises toward Stan's",
    x = "Season",
    y = "Share of all recorded dialogue",
    color = "Character",
    caption = "Source: southparkr transcript data; each season is normalized by its total recorded lines."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(randy_stan_plot, tooltip = "text")
```

In seasons 1-7, Randy averages `r round(randy_early_share, 1)`% of recorded lines, compared with Stan's `r round(stan_early_share, 1)`%. By seasons 15-21, Randy's average rises to `r round(randy_later_share, 1)`%, while Stan's falls to `r round(stan_later_share, 1)`%. In the later period, their dialogue shares are nearly equal.

## Why it matters

Randy's rising prominence suggests that the show's narrative focus expanded beyond the boys' experiences to give more space to adult and family perspectives. The change also overlaps with seasons that experimented with continuing storylines, including [season 18](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Park_(season_18)) and [season 20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Park_(season_20)). That timing offers context, but this chart cannot show that serialization or social satire caused Randy's rise. Dialogue share measures who speaks, not screen time or story importance.

## Beyond the data

The transcripts end at season 21, so they do not include season 22. That boundary matters: season 22 introduced Tegridy Farms, giving Randy an ongoing storyline largely independent of the boys. It is a later example of Randy-centered storytelling, not something this dataset can measure. See the [season 22 overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Park_(season_22)) and [South Park: Randy on Prime Video](https://www.primevideo.com/detail/South-Park-Randy/0MJAY5B8UONN6KYPMLCJZV8UL8).
